event_data.summary:
Projects can currently rely on guidance for final reviews without a durable mechanical gate that proves the required reviews actually happened for the exact work being delivered. This can allow incomplete or stale review evidence to accompany task completion or delivery.

Add an opt-in development-system policy that prevents an implementation ticket from being completed or delivered until three consecutive independent final reviews have found no substantive issues for the declared change scope. The evidence must be durable, machine-checkable, and stored through Tiber, the existing task authority. Developers must receive precise diagnostics about missing or invalid evidence, and any deliberate bypass must be explicit and auditable.

This matters because teams need completion and delivery claims to be backed by repeatable evidence rather than agent instructions alone, while retaining a deliberate project-level choice about adoption.

Implementation notes

Record review identity and type, exact scope or commit range, outcome, evidence, and timestamp. Reset the accepted clean sequence after a substantive finding, implementation mutation, declared-scope expansion, or relevant verification-evidence change. Gate ordinary local completion and continuous-integration delivery paths for both Codex and Claude configurations without depending on one model provider. Add black-box coverage for successful completion, missing-review rejection, every required reset class, and delivery blocking. Document configuration and migration behavior. Do not modify consumer repositories; capture any consumer configuration as follow-up work.
event_data.title: Require verified final reviews before work can finish
